title: Notely 3 review: quick to search, thin on the free plan
metaDescription: Notely 3 searched a 4,200-note vault in under a second in my testing, but the free plan caps you at two devices. Here is who it suits.
excerpt: I moved 4,200 notes into Notely 3 and used it as my only note app for three weeks. Search is genuinely fast. The free plan is too tight to recommend.

updates.note: Re-checked both prices and added the yearly plan.

verdict.summary: Notely 3 is the fastest note app I have tested on a large vault, and the Markdown export means you are not locked in. But the free plan limits you to two devices and 100MB, which most people will outgrow within months, so treat the £3.99 a month plan as the real price.
bestFor: People with thousands of existing notes who want fast search
Anyone who wants plain Markdown files they can take elsewhere
skipIf: You need to share notes with a team, which it cannot do
You want handwriting or stylus support on a tablet

sections.heading: What Notely 3 actually is
sections.body:
Notely is a local-first note app. Your notes live as Markdown files on your own disk, and the paid plan syncs them between devices through the company's servers.

The third version, released this year, replaced the search index. That is the change I wanted to test, because search was the reason I had avoided the app before.

sections.heading: Search stayed under a second on 4,200 notes
sections.body:
I imported a vault of 4,200 notes, about 180MB, and ran the same 20 searches I use on every note app I test. The median result came back in 0.4 seconds, and the slowest was 1.1 seconds on a three-word phrase.

For comparison, the same vault and the same searches took a median of 2.1 seconds in the app I had been using. That difference is large enough to change how you work: I started searching instead of filing things into folders.

table.caption: Search times on the same 4,200-note vault

sections.heading: It lost two notes in three weeks
sections.body:
Twice, edits I made on Android with no signal did not survive. On 14 October I edited a note on the Tube, and on 17 October I did the same. Both times the note reverted to its earlier version once the phone reconnected, and I only noticed because I keep a nightly backup.

Two notes out of 4,200 is a small proportion, but silent data loss in a note app is the one failure that matters. I reported both. If you work offline often, wait for a fix.

sections.heading: The free plan is not the real price
sections.body:
The free plan allows two devices and 100MB. I passed 100MB during the import alone, and two devices means a laptop and a phone with nothing left over for a work machine.

So judge Notely at £3.99 a month, or £39 a year, both checked on 24 October 2026. At that price it competes with apps that do more, and the lack of any sharing feature becomes harder to accept.

alternatives.name: Plain Markdown files and ripgrep
alternatives.why: Free, nothing to lose, and about as fast if you are comfortable in a terminal. No sync, which you would set up yourself.

alternatives.name: Kestrel Notes
alternatives.why: Slower search, but it has team sharing and I saw no data loss in testing.

faq.a: Yes on desktop, where notes are local files. On Android I lost two offline edits during three weeks of testing, so I would not rely on it offline until that is fixed.

faq.q: Can I get my notes out?
faq.a: Yes. A full export of 4,200 notes to Markdown took 73 seconds and the 50 notes I spot-checked kept their images and links intact.
Only for a small vault on two devices. A 180MB import exceeded the 100MB free limit on its own, so most people moving an existing vault will need the paid plan.
